sections.skill: Choose a savings account and explain how deposit insurance protects deposits

questions.prompt: Why do people usually keep money for a goal six months away in a savings account rather than in checking?

choices.text: Savings usually earns more and stays apart from spending money
Savings accounts cannot be withdrawn from until the goal date
Checking accounts are not insured by the FDIC
Savings accounts guarantee the money will double

questions.correct_answer: Savings usually earns more and stays apart from spending money
questions.intro: A savings account is a deposit account for money you are setting aside. It usually pays more interest than checking, and keeping savings separate makes it less likely you will spend it by accident. You can generally withdraw when you need to, though some banks limit how often.
questions.feedback: Savings earns more and keeps goal money apart from spending money. Both checking and savings are deposits that can be insured.

misconceptions.B: Confuses savings with a certificate of deposit
misconceptions.D: Confuses saving with a guaranteed high return

sources: FDIC: Deposit insurance covers up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category; investment products are not deposits and are not FDIC insured. (https://www.fdic.gov/resources/deposit-insurance)

questions.prompt: A savings account pays 3.5% interest per year. About how much interest will $1,600 earn in one year?
questions.intro: Interest for one year ≈ balance × annual rate (as a decimal). To write a percent as a decimal, divide by 100: 3.5% = 0.035.

misconceptions.D: Gives the new balance instead of the interest

sources: FDIC: Deposit insurance covers up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category; investment products are not deposits and are not FDIC insured. (https://www.fdic.gov/resources/deposit-insurance)

questions.prompt: Grace has $300,000 in one individual savings account at a single FDIC-insured bank. If the bank failed, how much of her deposit would be above the standard insurance limit?
questions.intro: The FDIC insures deposits at insured banks up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category (such as individual or joint). Credit union deposits have the same coverage through the NCUA. No depositor has lost insured funds since the FDIC began in 1934.
questions.feedback: $300,000 − $250,000 = $50,000 is above the standard limit for one owner at one bank in one category.

misconceptions.A: Thinks every dollar is always insured
misconceptions.C: Confuses the insured part with the uninsured part

sources: FDIC: Deposit insurance covers up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category; investment products are not deposits and are not FDIC insured. (https://www.fdic.gov/resources/deposit-insurance)

questions.prompt: Leo buys shares of a stock mutual fund through an investment desk inside his bank's branch. The fund loses value. Does FDIC insurance cover the loss?

choices.text: Yes: anything bought at an FDIC-insured bank is insured
Yes, up to $250,000 of investment losses
Only if Leo paid for the fund with money from his checking account
No: investments are not deposits, even when sold at a bank

questions.correct_answer: No: investments are not deposits, even when sold at a bank
questions.intro: FDIC insurance covers deposits: checking, savings, money market deposit accounts, and certificates of deposit. It does not cover stocks, bonds, mutual funds, crypto assets, annuities, or life insurance, even if a bank sells them. It also does not protect against investment losses.
questions.feedback: Mutual funds are investments, not deposits, so FDIC insurance does not cover their losses.

misconceptions.B: Applies the deposit limit to market losses
misconceptions.C: Thinks the source of money changes coverage

questions.prompt: Ava needs money she can reach quickly for unexpected costs and does not want it to lose value. Which place fits best?

choices.text: A stock fund that has risen sharply this year
A 5-year certificate of deposit with a penalty for early withdrawal
Cash hidden in her bedroom
An insured savings account

questions.feedback: An insured savings account keeps money safe, available, and earning some interest.

misconceptions.A: Chooses past performance over safety and access
misconceptions.C: Ignores theft, loss, and lost interest

questions.prompt: Which money belongs in savings rather than checking?

choices.text: Money set aside for a laptop you plan to buy next spring
Money for this week's groceries
Money to pay this month's phone bill when it arrives next week
Cash for lunch tomorrow

questions.correct_answer: Money set aside for a laptop you plan to buy next spring
questions.intro: Checking is for money you will spend soon: bills and everyday purchases. Savings is for money you are setting aside for later: goals and emergencies.
questions.feedback: Money for a later goal belongs in savings.
sources: FDIC: Deposit insurance covers up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category; investment products are not deposits and are not FDIC insured. (https://www.fdic.gov/resources/deposit-insurance)

questions.prompt: Leila earns 2% interest on her $500 savings for a year. What does "earning interest" mean here?

choices.text: The bank adds money to her account
The bank charges her 2% to hold her money
She owes the bank $10
Her $500 is locked until she turns 18

questions.correct_answer: The bank adds money to her account
questions.intro: Interest on savings is money the bank pays you for keeping your money there. It is added to your balance.
questions.feedback: 2% of $500 is $10, which the bank adds to her account.

misconceptions.B: Confuses interest earned with a fee

questions.prompt: Which statement is TRUE about money in an insured savings account?

choices.text: It always grows faster than prices rise
It can be withdrawn with no limits of any kind at every bank in the country
It earns the same interest at every bank
Its value in dollars does not go down because of market changes

questions.correct_answer: Its value in dollars does not go down because of market changes
questions.feedback: Insured deposits do not lose dollars to market swings, though inflation can still reduce what the money buys.

questions.prompt:
Two savings accounts show:
Bank A: interest rate 4.00%, compounded monthly; APY 4.07%
Bank B: APY 4.05%
Which number should Mo use to compare them fairly?

choices.text: The APY of each account
The interest rate of Bank A and the APY of Bank B
The interest rate of each, ignoring APY
Whichever number is printed larger in the ad

questions.intro: The interest rate is the yearly rate before compounding. APY (annual percentage yield) shows what you actually earn in a year once interest is added to your balance and itself earns interest (compounding). Banks must show APY for savings, so use APY to compare accounts.
questions.feedback: APY includes compounding, so comparing APY to APY is fair. Bank A (4.07%) earns slightly more than Bank B (4.05%).
sources: FDIC: Deposit insurance covers up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category; investment products are not deposits and are not FDIC insured. (https://www.fdic.gov/resources/deposit-insurance)

questions.prompt: An account has an APY of 4.07%. About how much will $2,000 earn in one year if the rate stays the same and nothing is withdrawn?
questions.intro: APY is the actual percent your money grows in one year, so one year of earnings ≈ balance × APY.

misconceptions.D: Gives the balance, not the interest

questions.prompt: Why is APY usually a little higher than the stated interest rate?

choices.text: Banks add a bonus to every account
APY includes extra deposits you plan to make later in the year
APY is the rate before taxes are added
Interest that is added during the year also earns interest

questions.correct_answer: Interest that is added during the year also earns interest
questions.intro: APY (annual percentage yield) is the percent your money actually grows in one year. The stated interest rate is the yearly rate before compounding.
questions.feedback: With compounding, earlier interest earns interest too, so the yearly yield is above the stated rate.
sources: FDIC: Deposit insurance covers up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category; investment products are not deposits and are not FDIC insured. (https://www.fdic.gov/resources/deposit-insurance)

questions.prompt: A savings rate is "variable." What does that mean?

choices.text: The bank can change the rate over time
The rate is fixed until the account is closed
The rate depends on how many times you log in
The rate is negative in some months

questions.correct_answer: The bank can change the rate over time
questions.intro: Most savings accounts have variable rates: the bank can raise or lower them, often when market interest rates change. A certificate of deposit usually locks a rate for its term.
questions.feedback: Variable means the bank may change it; past or advertised rates are not promises.

sections.skill: Deposit insurance limits and ownership categories

questions.prompt: Marcus has $200,000 in an individual account at Bank A and $200,000 in an individual account at Bank B. Both banks are FDIC insured and separate. How much of his money is insured?
questions.intro: The $250,000 limit applies per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category. Money at two different banks is insured separately. (Two "brands" of the same bank are one bank for insurance purposes.)
questions.feedback: Each bank insures his $200,000 individually: $400,000 total.

misconceptions.C: Applies one limit across different banks
misconceptions.A: Thinks large balances are never insured

sources: FDIC: Deposit insurance covers up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category; investment products are not deposits and are not FDIC insured. (https://www.fdic.gov/resources/deposit-insurance)

questions.prompt: Sam and Pat own a joint account with $500,000 at one insured bank. Joint accounts are insured up to $250,000 per co-owner. How much is insured?
questions.intro: Joint accounts are a separate ownership category from individual accounts. Each co-owner's share of joint accounts at one bank is insured up to $250,000.
questions.feedback: Two co-owners × $250,000 = $500,000 of coverage, which covers the whole balance.

misconceptions.B: Applies one limit to the whole joint account

questions.prompt: Which product is covered by FDIC insurance when bought at an insured bank?

choices.text: Shares of an index fund
A cryptocurrency purchase
The contents of a safe deposit box
A 12-month certificate of deposit

questions.feedback: CDs are deposits. Investments, crypto assets, and safe deposit box contents are not insured deposits.

misconceptions.A: Thinks funds sold at banks are insured
misconceptions.B: Thinks crypto at a bank is insured

sources: FDIC: Deposit insurance covers up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category; investment products are not deposits and are not FDIC insured. (https://www.fdic.gov/resources/deposit-insurance)

questions.prompt: A website for a company that sells crypto says, "Your funds are safe — like a bank." What should a careful saver conclude?

choices.text: The funds must be FDIC insured
The company is a federally chartered bank
The NCUA insures every crypto platform that operates in the United States
That claim does not mean the funds are FDIC insured

questions.correct_answer: That claim does not mean the funds are FDIC insured
questions.intro: Only deposits at FDIC-insured banks (or NCUA-insured credit unions) are covered by deposit insurance. The FDIC warns consumers about companies that misrepresent their products as FDIC insured.
questions.feedback: Comparisons to banks are not insurance. Check the FDIC's BankFind tool to see if an institution is an insured bank, and remember crypto assets are not deposits.

misconceptions.A: Treats a comparison as a guarantee

sources: FDIC: Deposit insurance covers up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category; investment products are not deposits and are not FDIC insured. (https://www.fdic.gov/resources/deposit-insurance)

questions.prompt: Ella has $260,000 in one individual account at an insured bank and wants all of it insured. Which change would accomplish that most directly?

choices.text: Move $10,000 or more to an account at a different insured bank
Split it into two individual accounts at the same bank
Ask the bank to raise her personal limit
Withdraw the extra $10,000 and invest it in stocks for added safety

questions.correct_answer: Move $10,000 or more to an account at a different insured bank
questions.feedback: Coverage is per bank per category. Two individual accounts at the same bank share one $250,000 limit; a second bank adds coverage.

misconceptions.B: Thinks multiple accounts in one category add coverage
